answer:
The conventional file name is `REPO.md`. You share the repository page, which lives under `Repository/`, for example `Repository/myuser`, to a GitHub repo under that name. Each pointer needs two keys: `name`, a descriptive name for the library, and `uri`, the URI to install it from. `description`, `author` and `website` are recommended but optional.

This comes from `Library/Development.md`, in its "Create a repository" section.

Their purpose is to offer a curated list of libraries to install. / By default, SilverBullet ships with two repositories: [[^Repositories/Std]] with a curated selection of community libraries, and [[^Repositories/SilverBulletMD]] with optional libraries maintained by the SilverBullet project.   Terms: Let’s define terms: / The [[Library]] is the **unit of distribution**, typically implemented as [[Meta Page]]. Most libraries will be implemented in a single page (e.g. with a big [[Space Lua]] block), but more elaborate libraries may span multiple pages, some may wrap [[Plugs]]. / A [[Repository]] is a **discovery and curation mechanism** for libraries. They are collections of _pointers_ of _where_ to find libraries to install. SilverBullet ships with the [[^Repositories/Std]] and [[^Repositories/SilverBulletMD]] repositories, but you can install additional ones. / [[Share]] is the general-purpose mechanism built into SilverBullet to both _push_, _pull_ and _sync_ content in your space with the outside world. In the context of Libraries this mechanism is used (partially under the hood, but you’ll recognize traces of it) both for you to _publish_ your libraries, as well as to _install_ and _update_ other people’s creations.

  The Shared Pages view lists every page in your space that is [[Share|shared]], in four groups: / * **Pages**: pages you push, pull or sync. / * **Collections**: your [[Share/Collection|collections]], each with its number of pages and its target (in a narrow sidebar the target may not fit), and its member pages under it. When a collection’s `pages` function fails, the error is shown under it instead. / * **Libraries**: installed [[Library|libraries]]. / * **Repositories**: installed library repositories. / Open it with ${widgets.commandButton("Navigate: Shared Pages")}. It opens in the right sidebar. From its dock menu you can move it to the left sidebar, the bottom panel or a modal. Each row shows the page’s status. Clicking a row opens the page.

# Create a repository
If you develop a few libraries, it may be good to make them more discoverable. To do so, you can group them in a [[Repository|Repository]].

For this, create another page in your space, this time under `Repository/`, e.g. `Repository/myuser` and tag it with `#meta/repository`.

In the page body, put a list of all your libraries, encoded as [[Tag/data|data objects]] as follows:

    ---
    tags: meta/repository
    ---
    This is my curated list of awesome libraries!

    ```#meta/library/remote
    name: Library1
    description: This is my first awesome library
    website: http://url.com/to/docs
    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library1.md
    ---
    name: Library2
    description: This is my second awesome library
    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library2.md
    ```

Required keys are:
* `name`: a descriptive name of your library.
  **Note**: this name is _not_ used as an installation location, the installation location is determined by the `name` key in the library itself.
* `uri`: The URI to install the library from.

Additional recommended keys are:
* `description`: a more elaborate description of the library and its functionality
* `author`: who developed this library
* `website`: a website URL for more information

Now share this repo page using [[Share]] to the same github repo (or any other, it doesn’t really matter), and call it `REPO.md` (by convention).

Then announce to the [community](https://community.silverbullet.md/c/plugs-libraries/14) that your repo is open for business and they can add it via the `Library: Add Repository` command (using the same `share.uri` set in your frontmatter).
